prompts.head:
Use case: compositing. Asset type: editorial artwork installation-detail photograph for an artist portfolio.
Input image 1 is the artist's actual high-resolution artwork: it is the authoritative source for ALL colored marks, shapes, anatomy, registration offsets and proportions. Input image 2 is the existing installation photograph, authoritative for framing, mounting, wall and gallery lighting.
Make a convincingly photographic closeup of this actual drawing as physically installed in that reference gallery. Preserve the exact existing drawing, including its fluorescent orange, yellow and magenta layers; DO NOT redesign the artwork or invent drawing marks. These are flat drawings on white fine-art paper float-mounted inside narrow white-painted rectangular frames, on an off-white wall, not sculptural bones. Preserve fine drawing/print grain. Show tactile paper with a slight natural unevenness, understated edge shadow, recessed mounting, a narrow white frame rail and a little softly lit gallery wall so the result unmistakably reads as a photograph of installed physical art. Restrained neutral gallery daylight, soft shadows, accurate fluorescent colors with the slightly richer saturation and lower white exposure seen in the installation photo. Subtle oblique camera perspective from one side, professionally photographed on a 70mm lens; depth of field keeps drawing legible with only the far frame/wall slightly softer. No dramatic glare, no fake thick impasto, no canvas weave, no extra marks, no people, no labels, no typography, no watermark. A single landscape photograph, aspect ratio 3:2, high resolution. No collage or page layout.
Composition: tightly frame the Smilodon skull and long saber teeth with the open lower jaw. The skull fills most of the photo; crop the large blank top and bottom areas of the raw artwork. Keep the skull's orientation facing right and all its distinctive layered color shapes. Show the RIGHT white frame rail close to the image edge with a slim strip of gallery wall beyond it, and the paper's right edge, enough to make its physical installation unmistakable. The frame's top and bottom are outside the crop.
